premises.text: Economic and technological conditions now resemble the PC shift that made computers personal
premises.evidence_span: the conditions today, economical and technological, are very similar to different revolutions that moved us from these computers, large, expensive, difficult to use, to these computers, personal and in every home

premises.text: Smartphone and cloud robotics offload computation from the robot, making it affordable and dynamically upgradable
premises.evidence_span: smartphone robotics and cloud robotics that takes a computation from the robot into devices you already have, making it much more affordable, and also automatically and dynamically upgradable

premises.text: Task-limited home robots can enter affordably, unlike Swiss-army-knife robots costing hundreds of thousands
premises.evidence_span: move from Swiss army knife kind of robots that do anything from saving princesses to cleaning the house, but unfortunately cost hundreds of thousands of dollars. We're going to have a set of robots that are much more targeted at limited set of tasks

premises.text: Shimmy is a smartphone-powered, cloud-connected robotic speaker that listens to and engages with music
premises.evidence_span: smartphone-powered, cloud-connected robot. called Shimmy. And Shimmy is a robotic speaker dog that doesn't just play the music for you. It actually listens to it and enjoys it as much as you do

premises.text: Dumb-robot architecture: motors, speakers, and power, with all intelligence on a smartphone app and the cloud
premises.evidence_span: everything that the robot does actually happens on a smartphone app and on the cloud. And the robot is just some motors, high-end speakers, and power

premises.text: Cloud music structure data drives real-time choreography computed on the Android device
premises.evidence_span: taking information from the cloud that has the beats, the segments, where the chorus starts, where the verse starts, what genre the song is. And it creates a real-time live choreography for this, which is different every time you play a different song, which is all computed on the Android device

premises.text: Phone-camera face tracking keeps the robot oriented for the best sound
premises.evidence_span: using the camera to track my faces, always pointing towards me and giving me the best sound possible

premises.text: Consumer price is about $199, with early Kickstarter at $149
premises.evidence_span: able to get it to $199. And if you are very quick and early adopters, like most of you are, we started a Kickstarter campaign that today you can get it for the next month for $149

value.text: Engaging, affordable, fun personal robots in the home
value.evidence_span: engaging, affordable, and fun to use robots in the home

causal_links.evidence_span: take the promise of a robot in every home and make it a reality
Shimmy is a robotic speaker dog that doesn't just play the music for you

notes: Singleton D3 retained: consumer price/Kickstarter is a separately revisable commercial condition. Price amount and Kickstarter early-adopter channel kept as one commercial premise per v1.3.1 §4.1.3. Demo failures and financing narrative excluded.
